findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND, and the r4 blocker is closed: the reset alternative is gone and the clause now forbids repo reuse plainly enough that a checker would not do it anyway. I rebuilt the r4 attack from scratch rather than replaying it -- one repo, `git reset --hard` plus `git clean -xdff` between cases, table run in order, correct guard -- and reproduced every consequence r4 named, which is what makes the deletion load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Under reuse the markers accumulate and HEAD stays detached from case A onward, so a CORRECT guard reports REBASE on D1 and D2 (V-2 fails correct work) and the merge-detector mutation leaves D1 and D2 at exit 1 (V-1 reports a live merge detector as dead, and a guard with no merge detector is indistinguishable from one that has it). Under fresh-repo-per-case all of it comes out right. The text at :98 leaves no second reading: it states the rule, states there is no alternative, and then gives both independent reasons in the paragraph that follows, including the .git/ one the deleted recipe could not satisfy.
findings.evidence: Measured, baseline 298c8a6, PATH="$STUBS:/usr/bin:/bin", $STUBS and $HOME outside the repo, dates pinned through setup, date and osascript stubbed. REUSE (the deleted recipe), correct guard: A1/A2 markers=[] SAID=detached; B1/B2 markers=[rebase-merge] SAID=rebase; C1/C2 markers=[rebase-merge,rebase-apply] SAID=rebase; D1/D2 markers=[rebase-merge,rebase-apply,MERGE_HEAD] SAID=rebase (V-2 requires merge); every case detached=True from A onward. REUSE, no-merge mutation: D1 exit=1, D2 exit=1, neither flips. FRESH repo per case, correct guard: all nine exit=1, counts 1->1 (E1 2->2), staged unchanged, said = detached/detached/rebase/rebase/rebase/rebase/merge/merge/rebase, osascript 1 call per case, 6/6 phase headings, no 'Nothing to commit' anywhere. FRESH, no-merge mutation: D1 exit=0 cnt 1->2, D2 exit=0 -- both flip, nothing else moves. constitution.md:98-100.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: the fresh-repo table still catches the r2/r3 defective guard and still costs a correct one nothing. Rebuilt rather than trusted: a guard identical to the correct one except placed after the clean-tree exit at :130-133 clears the five dirty cases and is caught on all four clean ones by the plain exit!=0 assertion, with no reliance on the porcelain reading. All three per-detector mutations flip exactly their own cases and leave the other six alone, so each detector is independently load-bearing as the clause claims.
findings.evidence: Measured, fresh repo per case. DEFECTIVE (guard after :133): A1=1, A2=0, B1=1, B2=0, C1=1, C2=0, D1=1, D2=0, E1=1 -- four clean cases violate exit!=0. MUTATION no-detached: A1 exit=0 cnt 1->2, A2 exit=0, B/C/D/E unchanged at exit=1. MUTATION no-rebase: B1 exit=0 cnt 1->2, B2/C1/C2 flip, A/D hold, E1 falls back to the detached string. MUTATION no-merge: D1 exit=0 cnt 1->2, D2 exit=0, rest hold. constitution.md:110.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND: the porcelain precondition now voids in both directions (:102), which closes the r4 minor. The reachable path r4 named -- B-4's control committing A1's dirty marker away and leaving a later case clean in name only -- is closed twice over now, since the control also gets its own repo. I checked the opposite hole too: the precondition still cannot be used to wave off a genuine artifact failure, because it reads one pre-run datum on a repo built moments earlier, and the correct and defective guards produce a byte-identical pre-run porcelain column.
findings.evidence: Measured, fresh repos: pre-run porcelain empty on A2/B2/C2/D2 and ['?? drift.txt'] on the five dirty cases, identical under the correct and the after-clean-tree-exit guard. constitution.md:102 ('or a dirty case shows nothing, the run is void'), :98 ('B-4's two-sided control gets its own repo too').

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND, claim by claim rather than by assertion: with DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH unset the script takes the opt-in branch at :159 exactly as it ships, and an additive flip of that default is visible to V-4's stream comparison. Pinning the variable to 0 -- the instinct the clause now heads off -- makes the same flip byte-identical and invisible. So naming it in the stub contract really does convert that coverage from an unstated harness choice into a property of the document.
findings.evidence: Measured, attached-dirty, harness otherwise identical, dates pinned through setup. Var UNSET, baseline last lines: '==> Committed locally. Auto-push is off; push manually:  git -C "SCRATCH" push'. Same script plus an inserted `: "${DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH:=1}"` (1 added line, 0 removed): '==> Pushing to origin' / 'd6ed8bf..9d2b8f1  main -> main' / '==> Done...' -- streams DIFFER, caught. Var exported as 0: streams IDENTICAL, invisible. dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync:159; constitution.md:180.

findings.description: VERIFIED SOUND and load-bearing: the clause is new, so I built both escapes fresh and confirmed first that they really are invisible to everything else, then that D-4's rubric rejects them. Committed on clones of 298c8a6 alongside a correct guard, the added elif arm in the push-failure classifier and the brew-gated phase writing into $SRC both keep D-1 part 1 at the allowlisted path, return 0 removed lines for part 3, produce zero B-1 pattern matches, and leave V-4 byte-identical on both the dirty and the clean attached run. D-4's text forbids each by name ('no new phase ... no edit to the push-failure classifier') and its check names both as measured examples, so two checkers would rule the same way on these two. No vacuity from overlap: D-4 is judgment where D-1 is mechanical, they gate different failure classes, and neither can be satisfied by the other passing.
findings.evidence: Measured on clones of 298c8a6, each variant committed. correct guard alone: paths=['dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync'], removed=0 added=16, B-1 rc=1, V-4 identical dirty+clean. +elif arm: removed=0 added=18, B-1 rc=1, V-4 identical dirty+clean. +brew-gated phase: removed=0 added=19, B-1 rc=1, V-4 identical dirty+clean. +`: "${DOTFILES_AUTO_PUSH:=1}"`: removed=0 added=17, B-1 rc=1, V-4 identical CLEAN but DIFFERS dirty (caught by V-4, per the B-4 finding above). constitution.md:199-204.

findings.description: The one substantive finding of this round, and the only absence-only check in the document with no positive control behind it. B-1's whole verdict rides on `grep -E` exiting 1 over the added lines, so every way the pipeline can go inert -- wrong pattern, wrong path, empty input -- reads as PASS. That is exactly the reasoning B-4's two-sided control and B-3's 'a case that stays green is measuring nothing' already encode elsewhere in this document; B-1 is the clause that never got it. And there is a concrete, one-invisible-character way in: the pattern is reproduced in a fenced block inside a bullet list, so in the raw file it carries two leading spaces, and copied that way it matches NOTHING -- including B-1's own failing example. The clause does say 'tests/lint.bats's own pattern verbatim', which points at the authoritative copy, and dedented it is byte-identical to lint.bats:50; a checker who extracts from the file is fine. A checker who pastes the block is silently inert and reports PASS. What escapes is narrow, which is why this is a major and not a blocker: the guard would still have to clear V-1's nine cases, V-2, V-3 and V-4, so a behaviourally broken guard is caught regardless -- I could not construct one that survives. What ships is a bare-compound style violation of a blocker clause, latent rather than active, and B-1 is the only thing covering it because lint.bats does not scan this file. Fix is one sentence in the clause's own vocabulary: before trusting a zero-match result, confirm the pattern matches this clause's failing example; if it does not, the check is inert and the run is void.
findings.evidence: Measured. Pattern as it appears in the raw file at constitution.md:150 ('  (^[[:space:]]*|;...') vs tests/lint.bats:50: identical after stripping the two-space fence indent, differing with it. grep -nE over five sample added lines: dedented -> rc=0, matches 4 of 5 including '[[ -z "$(git symbolic-ref -q HEAD)" ]] && guard=1' (B-1's own failing example) and '  (( retries++ ))'; indented -> rc=1, ZERO matches, which is B-1's stated pass condition. tests/lint.bats:38 confirms lint's scanned surface is $BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/*.bats plus helpers.bash plus mutation-check.sh, and tests/mutation-check.sh:67 hardcodes six files -- neither reaches dot_local/bin/executable_dotfiles-sync, so nothing else covers this. constitution.md:147-153.

findings.description: The r4 minor is closed for the control-versus-V-1 boundary, but not inside the control itself: ':98 says the control gets its own repo, singular, and B-4 :185 asks the positive half to run against case A1 and the negative half against case A2 without saying they are different repos. Sharing one is the natural economy, because after the positive half the repo is detached and clean, which IS the A2 construction. Measured, that reading destroys the negative half's only diagnostic power for pre-run dirt: with $STUBS placed inside the scratch repo, the positive half commits `stubs/` away, so the negative half sees a clean tree, prints 'Nothing to commit' and passes. Two repos catches it. Minor rather than major because the coverage is genuinely complementary: pre-run dirt is caught by V-1's porcelain precondition anyway, and mid-run dirt -- the `code` hazard this clause names -- is caught by the negative half whether or not the repos are shared, since the dirtying happens during the run being measured. One phrase ('each half against a repo the other has not touched') closes it.
findings.evidence: Measured, baseline script, $STUBS INSIDE the repo. Halves share one repo: positive A1 exit=0 commit created; negative on the same repo exit=0, 'Nothing to commit' present -> control PASSES, leak hidden, porcelain before the negative half = 0 entries. Each half its own repo: negative A2 pre-porcelain = ['?? stubs/'], exit=0, 'Nothing to commit' ABSENT -> control FAILS, leak caught. V-1 independently: pre-run porcelain on A2/B2/C2/D2 all ['?? stubs/'] -> precondition voids the run. Mid-run case (`code` resolving with $SRC/dot_config present, nominally clean A2): correct and defective guards both exit 1 with pre-porcelain empty -- V-1's precondition blind -- while the baseline negative control commits (cnt 2->3) and prints no 'Nothing to commit', catching it. constitution.md:98, :185.

findings.description: B-3 imports one of V-1's construction rules into the committed cases and not the other. It requires any merge case to be built with `git rev-parse HEAD > .git/MERGE_HEAD` 'for the reason V-1 gives', but says nothing about repo isolation -- and V-1's other reason applies verbatim to the worker's bats file, because B-3 then runs the same three per-detector mutations over it. A test file that shares one fixture repo across its four cases hits the failure I measured above: the merge case stays red under the merge mutation because the earlier cases' .git/rebase-* markers survive, so B-3 reports a working detector as dead. It fails safe -- the verdict is FAIL, not a false PASS -- so this costs a rework round rather than admitting anything, which is why it is a minor. Half a sentence ('each case builds its own repo, for the reason V-1 gives') would spend the retry budget on the guard instead.
findings.evidence: Same mechanism measured under V-1 above: reused repo, correct guard, no-merge mutation -> D1 exit=1, D2 exit=1, neither flips; fresh repos -> both flip. `git reset --hard` plus `git clean -xdff` leaves .git/rebase-merge and .git/rebase-apply in place. constitution.md:167-169 (the imported MERGE_HEAD rule, no isolation rule), :98-100 (the reason).

findings.description: A residual of exactly the species D-4 was just written to close, one file over. D-1 part 3's no-removed-lines rule is scoped to the script, and nothing takes an equivalent reading of `tests/`, so an assertion deleted from inside an existing test case is invisible to the whole document: the per-file @test floor counts test blocks rather than assertions, the skip check looks for added skips rather than removed asserts, and dropping an assertion cannot turn a green test red. Low likelihood -- the job's cases can live in new files and B-3 explicitly allows that -- but the cost of closing it is a fourth bullet in D-2's check ('git diff 298c8a6..HEAD -- tests/ removes no assertion line', or simply a removed-line count the checker eyeballs), and the cost of leaving it is that the suite this job is judged green against can be quietly weakened.
findings.evidence: Measured on a clone of 298c8a6 with `[ "$status" -eq 0 ]` deleted from the first case in tests/apps.bats and committed: /usr/bin/grep -c '^@test' tests/apps.bats -> 18 (floor holds), added-skip check -> 0 matches, D-1 part 1 paths -> ['tests/apps.bats'] (allowlisted), D-1 part 3 over the script -> 0. Only `git diff 298c8a6..HEAD -- tests/ | grep -c '^-[^-]'` -> 1 sees it, and no clause takes that reading. constitution.md:206-211, :195.

findings.description: Every external fact the document leans on, re-derived from the artifacts at 298c8a6 rather than carried forward from r4. All of it holds. Worth one note for the orchestrator: 298c8a6 is still the repo's HEAD with a clean tree, so 298c8a6..HEAD is empty today and every diff-scoped check starts from zero -- if commits land before the job starts, D-1 and D-2 silently inherit them.
findings.evidence: git rev-parse --short HEAD -> 298c8a6; git status --porcelain -> empty. Script is 182 lines: :16 set -euo pipefail, :26 the tee redirect, :28-31 notify, :33-36 notify_fail, phase headings at :39/:57/:65/:75/:85/:103, :128 cd "$SRC", :130-133 the clean-tree exit, :137 the bare compound (also :88, :122), :142 the date-bearing commit subject, :153-158 the push rationale, :159 the opt-in branch, :169-177 the classifier, :182 the last line. Floors by /usr/bin/grep -c '^@test': apps 18, doctor 11, font 44, install-failures 17, jsonc 9, licensed-fonts 7, lint 1, packages 13; bats --count tests/ = 120, so D-2's '>120' is a real floor. check-diff-scope.py on the clean tree -> 'OK: 0 path(s) in scope' rc=0, which is why D-1 part 1 cannot be dropped. B-4's claim about the `code` phase re-measured: the failed redirect prints 'No such file or directory' and the run continues to exit 0 under set -e, exactly as the clause says.

findings.description: Cold read, sixth audit, no history in hand: the document is coherent, no two clauses contradict, every clause carries a check a checker could actually run and a failing example I could build, and the two cold-read items r4 raised are folded into the new 'Notes for the worker' section rather than lost. Coverage against the spec's seven acceptance criteria is complete (AC1/AC4 -> V-1, AC2 -> V-2, AC3 -> V-3, AC5 -> V-4, AC6 -> V-5, AC7 -> B-3 plus D-2). Two cosmetics, neither worth a severity: D-4 is filed between D-1 and D-2 so the D-block reads 1, 4, 2, 3; and D-4 carries severity major while D-1, whose text it completes, is a blocker -- a new phase writing into the real source dir is not obviously the lesser fault.
findings.evidence: constitution.md:67-73 (the notes), :189-218 (the D block). Spec acceptance criteria at spec.md:60-66, each mapped above.
